### Findings (1)

**dangling-citation** (1)
- `backlog/x4omld5-mutation-check-operation-prove-a-guard-fails-when-its-bug-re.md:27` — Two resolved cards (x4omld5, xwp8ioh) each cite "#x2sqf62" as the prior instance of the same failure mode, but no backlog item with that hash id exists anywhere in current origin/main or in this PR's own branch history. — A future reader (or an automated citation sweep) follows the "#x2sqf62" reference expecting to find the backlog item that established the ~12%-stale-cards finding; it resolves nowhere, and the reader either wastes time hunting for a renamed/renumbered item (misdiagnosing it as a JIT-numbering bug, exactly the class xm1y7m2 in this same diff describes) or simply loses the citation's evidentiary trail. Verified: `git grep -l x2sqf62` against fetched real origin/main and the full history of this PR's own branch (web-everything/web-everything#1506) returns zero hits; I could not exhaustively check all other open lanes/branches, so this is reported with that caveat rather than as certain. No behavior/code is touched by this finding (pure prose), so the mutation-probe requirement does not apply — there is nothing to break or redden. _[PLAUSIBLE]_ _[impact if unfixed: cosmetic]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Extend check-standards' existing backlog citation-resolution scan (same dUnresolvedRef shape already used for parent/blockedBy/graduatedTo and we:-path loci) to also match `#[0-9]+`/`#x[0-9a-z]{6}` tokens in backlog item body prose and warn when they don't resolve to a known item. Note this diff already files a narrower, related gap (xm1y7m2, prose citations in docs/ going stale after JIT renumbering) but that card doesn't cover backlog-to-backlog prose citations, and neither is an implemented gate yet.
